question: She ___ in Pune for six years before she moved to Delhi.

question: By the time the police arrived, the thief ___.

question: I ___ for the bus for twenty minutes when it finally came.

question: You ___ told me earlier; I would have helped.

question: If it ___ tomorrow, we will cancel the picnic.
why: In a first conditional, the if-clause takes the simple present.

question: If I ___ the lottery, I would buy a farm.
why: A second conditional (unreal present) uses the past simple after if.

question: The streets are wet, so it ___ last night.
why: Must have plus the past participle shows a strong guess about the past.

question: If she had left earlier, she ___ the train.
why: A past unreal condition gives would have plus a past participle.

question: I wish I ___ the answer yesterday.
why: A wish about the past uses the past perfect.

question: The lights are on, so they ___ at home.
why: Must expresses a firm guess from evidence.

question: Had I known about the strike, I ___ at home.
why: Had I known is an inverted if I had known, so the result is would have plus participle.

question: By next March, Aarav ___ in this company for ten years.

question: It is high time we ___ the project.

question: ___ honest man never lies.

question: There is hardly ___ milk left.

question: She bought ___ umbrella yesterday.

question: He has two cars, but ___ of them is new.

why: Water is uncountable, so use much.

b: I want to sell my cycle because I am going to college and it is good, please call me.
c: FOR SALE: Hero cycle, two years old, gears work well, ₹3,500. Call 98765xxxxx after 5 pm.
why: A good ad gives the item, condition, price and contact in few words.

question: Which slogan best suits a poster on saving water?
a: Water is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen.
d: Every drop counts: close the tap!
why: A poster slogan is short, catchy and urges action.

question: Which is NOT needed in a notice about a change in bus timings?
a: A paragraph on the history of buses
c: The date from which it applies
why: A notice carries only the facts the reader needs.

chapter: Short Writing: Notices, Posters, Advertisements and Invitations
question: Which is the correct opening of a formal invitation?
a: Hey! Come to our Annual Day, it will be fun.
b: The Principal and staff of Sunrise Public School request the pleasure of your company at the Annual Day.
c: You must attend our Annual Day.
d: I invite you, yaar, to our Annual Day.
why: Formal invitations use polite third-person wording.

chapter: Short Writing: Notices, Posters, Advertisements and Invitations
question: Which detail is least necessary in a "Wanted: Receptionist" advertisement?
why: The ad should give job, qualification, pay and contact only.

chapter: Short Writing: Notices, Posters, Advertisements and Invitations
question: A poster urging people to get vaccinated should NOT
d: carry a long paragraph of statistics
why: Posters rely on brevity; long text defeats their purpose.

chapter: Short Writing: Notices, Posters, Advertisements and Invitations
question: Which set of details is the most complete for a blood donation camp notice?
c: Date, time, venue, who may donate and a contact person
why: A notice must answer what, when, where, who and whom to contact.

chapter: Short Writing: Notices, Posters, Advertisements and Invitations
question: In a formal invitation, "RSVP" should be followed by
d: a phone number or email to confirm attendance
why: RSVP asks guests to reply, so contact details are needed.

question: Which sentence is best in the body of a notice for a debate?
a: All students of classes XI and XII interested in the inter-house debate on 5 August at 11 a.m. in the auditorium should give their names to Mr Rao by 1 August.
b: Everybody should come to the debate sometime.
c: The debate will be very nice and fun.
why: It covers who, what, when, where and whom to contact.

chapter: Short Writing: Notices, Posters, Advertisements and Invitations
question: A student spends 20 of 50 words in a notice describing past events. The biggest risk is that
b: time, venue or contact details are left out
why: Limited words must go to essential details.

question: Which layout suits a poster on "Save Electricity"?
b: A letter with a salutation and closing
d: Bold heading, two short lines and the issuer's name at the bottom
why: A poster has a bold message, brief support and a source.

question: A formal reply accepting an invitation is best written in
a: the third person, like the invitation

question: A notice about an event on 9 September is written on 2 September. The date shown below the word NOTICE is
why: The notice date is when it is issued; the event date goes in the body.

question: Which salutation fits a letter to the Editor?
why: Formal letters use Dear Sir or Sir.

question: A newspaper report of an event is usually written in the ___ tense.
why: The event has already happened.

question: A newspaper report is written in the
why: Reports are impersonal and objective.

question: "Yours faithfully" is used when the letter begins with
why: Dear Sir (name unknown) pairs with Yours faithfully.

question: A byline in a report or article shows
why: The byline credits the writer.

question: The subject line of a formal letter should be
why: It tells the reader the purpose at a glance.

question: An article for a school magazine should have
c: a title and a clear introduction
why: Articles need a catchy title and an introduction.

question: A report on a school event should answer
why: A report states the main facts.

question: Which is the right order for a newspaper report?
why: A report opens with the headline, then the writer's name, then the facts.

question: Which is NOT normally part of an article?
why: A salutation belongs to a letter.

question: Best subject line for a letter complaining about late delivery of a washing machine ordered on 3 May:
a: Complaint about delayed delivery of washing machine ordered on 3 May
why: A good subject line states the topic, the problem and the key detail.

question: The introduction of an article should
b: catch interest and state the topic
why: The opening hooks the reader and sets the theme.

question: Which headline suits a report on a tree plantation drive?
b: A drive was done by students in school on a day
d: Why trees are good, a long essay
why: Headlines are short, specific and use strong verbs.

question: Which line suits a letter of enquiry to a coaching institute?
c: I will join tomorrow, keep a seat.
d: Kindly send me details of the course fee, duration and batch timings.
why: An enquiry asks politely for specific information.

question: Which closing suits a letter to the Editor?
why: A letter to the Editor is formal; use Yours faithfully.

question: Which is true of a report?
b: It states facts in an objective tone.
d: It is written as a dialogue.
why: Reports are formal and factual.

question: Which closing line is best for a complaint letter to a dealer?
a: I request you to replace the set within seven days, failing which I shall approach the consumer forum.
b: Fix it or I will ruin you.
why: It is firm, polite and states a deadline and consequence.

question: A job application letter that replies to an advertisement should begin by
b: referring to the advertisement and the post
why: The first line links the letter to the advertisement.

question: Which sentence is suitable in a newspaper report?
a: I felt the fair was awesome.
b: You must visit it next year.
c: The chief guest, Dr Anita Rao, inaugurated the fair, which drew over 2,000 visitors.
why: Reports name the people and give facts.

question: Which is the best ending for a job application letter?
b: Hire me or I will complain.
d: I shall be grateful for an opportunity to appear for an interview.
why: It is polite, formal and states the request.

question: Which order is best for an article on the importance of sleep?
a: Striking opening fact, effects, suggestions, conclusion
why: Articles move from an opening to development to a conclusion.

question: Which is NOT a feature of a good report?
b: Personal opinions in the first person
why: Reports stay objective.

question: Which is the most effective first paragraph for an article on road safety?
b: Hello readers, I am writing about roads.
c: Every year, over a lakh people die on Indian roads; most of these deaths can be prevented.
why: A strong fact and a hint of what follows hook the reader.

question: In a formal letter, the best way to state your complaint is to
d: state the problem factually and ask for a specific remedy
why: Formal complaints are polite, factual and ask for a remedy.
